additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 27 October 2026 against all 830 sites and 894 projects, the evidence records, source records and identity mapping of verified_construction_core/2026-10-27-research-ninetyninth (site/config.json read ninety-eighth at the start of this pass and ninety-ninth when the screen was repeated before finishing), every sources/*-holds.json file, all other queue fragments' changes and holds, and claims.tsv, for Green Mountain, LON-East, Romford, King George Close, RM7 7PN, Infinity, ISDC, EPR/FP3630EU, Havering, P1238.23 and P1029.26. No Atlas record, hold or queued change names this campus: the Atlas Green Mountain records are its Norwegian and Mainz campuses, and the 'King George' matches are King George County, Virginia. No Atlas site, queued addition or other claim lies within 2 km; the nearest Atlas sites are the Charlton data centre proposal (14.2 km) and the Telehouse London Docklands campus (14.4 km). locator.identity_review: The register names the permit holder Green Mountain DC UK Limited at 'Romford North Data Centre', King George Close, Romford; the Environment Agency's 29 April 2026 inspection report for the same permit records Green Mountain DC UK Limited as operator and discusses the new data halls' generators; Green Mountain's 8 June and 1 September 2026 releases identify its Romford campus as LON-East and say Green Mountain DC UK owns the eight-acre site; and Green Mountain's December 2023 release says the site came with Infinity Data Centres in January 2023 (consistent with the 'ISDC Development' premises name in the register address) and that the 14 MW expansion was built inside the existing building. Havering's permission P1238.23 for a fin wall to 'the existing data storage facility' at 3 King George Close carries a 3.47 ha polygon that contains the register point (shapely 2.1.1: 62 m inside, 22 m from its centroid). In Esri World Imagery viewed locally (not redistributed) the point falls on a large pale-roofed industrial building with rooftop plant and a southern plant yard. A pyproj 3.7.1 transform of the register's easting and northing lands 0.77 m from the published point, and the RM7 7PN postcode centroid is 88 m away, so the point is not a postcode default. No geocoder, town centre or estate centroid is used.
locator.precision: Site location published by the Environment Agency's installations register for permit EPR/FP3630EU (holder Green Mountain DC UK Limited, 'Romford North Data Centre, Unit 3 King George close, Romford, RM7 7PN'): grid reference TQ5027089800, latitude 51.587017, longitude 0.167675, copied without transformation. It lies inside Havering's 3.47 ha planning polygon for the existing data storage facility at 3 King George Close and locates the campus's existing building; it is not a building outline or surveyed position.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The register publishes no positional accuracy; the point lies inside the 3.47 ha existing-facility planning polygon, and the 14 MW data halls occupy part of the existing building around it, not a separately located structure.

status.summary: Green Mountain's release dated 1 September 2026 announces a customer agreement for 14 MW at its LON-East campus in Romford, East London, under which a neocloud operator will occupy 'the recently delivered 14 MW of AI-ready capacity'. This dated operator disclosure supports completed status, as of 1 September 2026, for the 14 MW expansion: in Green Mountain's December 2023 description, six data halls built in two 7 MW phases inside the existing building. Completion keeps that scope. The customer's occupation is future, so operation of the new capacity is not asserted, and the campus's 37 MW planned total, its legacy 7 MW operation and the planned further building across King George Close are outside this project.
